title: A Golden Coral So Strange It Got Its Own New Family
summary:
Deep in the Pacific Ocean near Costa Rica, scientists found a bright yellow coral that does not fit into any known coral family. So they made a brand-new family for it!

The coral grows in branches that look like trees. Some are more than a meter tall, which is over 3 feet. It lives between 360 and 529 meters deep, on underwater mountains called seamounts. Scientists used an underwater robot named SuBastian to collect samples.

The coral grows among brittle stars, which are relatives of starfish. The yellow branches looked like glowing trees surrounded by stars.

That gave scientists an idea for its name. They used Elvish, a language made up by J.R.R. Tolkien, who wrote "The Lord of the Rings." The name Laurinque means "golden tree," and elenya means "of the stars."

Scientists studied hundreds of the coral's genes to learn where it belongs. The discovery shows how much of the deep ocean is still unexplored.
why_it_matters: It shows there are still amazing animals waiting to be discovered in the deep ocean.
